record.original_question: Let C be one of the following matrix classes: (i) the class of matrices A_{n,k,t} for positive integers n and k and t in (0, 1), (ii) the class of GKK τ-matrices, (iii) the class of GKK matrices, or (iv) the class of τ-matrices. For each n, let C_n denote the subclass of matrices in C whose order is at most n. What is the largest integer n such that every matrix in C_n is stable, meaning that every eigenvalue has positive real part?

evidence.quote: For various classes C of matrices, this raises the following three questions concerning the subclass Cn of all matrices in C of order less than or equal to n.
3a. What is the maximum n such that all matrices in class Cn are stable?

Specific classes C of interest include i. The class of matrices An,k,t for positive integers n and k, and for t ∈ (0, 1), ii. The class of GKK τ -matrices, iii. The class of GKK matrices, iv. The class of τ -matrices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup and definitions.

(a) For a square matrix A with real entries, A is called stable (positive stable) if every eigenvalue of A has strictly positive real part.

(b) A real n×n matrix A is said to be weakly sign-symmetric if for every pair of index subsets α, β ⊆ {1,…,n} of equal cardinality with |α△β| ≤ 2, the product of the corresponding minors A[α|β]·A[β|α] is nonnegative. A real square matrix A is called a GKK matrix if every principal minor of A is positive and A is weakly sign-symmetric.

(c) A real square matrix A is called a τ-matrix if every principal minor of A is positive and, for every principal submatrix A[α] of A, the smallest real eigenvalue (the Perron-type root) of A[α] is at least the smallest real eigenvalue of A. (Equivalently, A is a nonsingular matrix whose principal minors are positive and which satisfies the eigenvalue-monotonicity property τ(A[α]) ≥ τ(A) for all principal submatrices, where τ(M) denotes the minimum of the real parts of the eigenvalues of M.) A GKK τ-matrix is a matrix that is simultaneously a GKK matrix and a τ-matrix.

(d) For positive integers n, k and a real parameter t ∈ (0,1), define the n×n Toeplitz–Hessenberg matrix A_{n,k,t} by
  (A_{n,k,t})_{ij} = 1 if i = j,
  (A_{n,k,t})_{ij} = −t^{(j−i+1)k} if j ≥ i+1 (entries above the diagonal arranged as in a Hessenberg/Toeplitz pattern with parameter t and exponent depending on k),
  (A_{n,k,t})_{ij} = c_{i−j} if i > j, where the subdiagonal entries are chosen so that the matrix lies in the τ-matrix / GKK class for the relevant ranges of parameters (the standard Toeplitz–Hessenberg construction parametrized by k and t producing GKK matrices for all t ∈ (0,1) and τ-matrices for n ≤ 2k+2 and small t > 0).

For a class C of square matrices, let C_n denote the set of all matrices in C of order at most n.

Question. For each of the following classes C, determine the largest integer n such that every matrix in C_n is stable:
 (i) C = the class of all matrices A_{n,k,t} with positive integers n, k and t ∈ (0,1);
 (ii) C = the class of all GKK τ-matrices;
 (iii) C = the class of all GKK matrices;
 (iv) C = the class of all τ-matrices.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work ("Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable") provided explicit unstable examples A_{2k+2,k,t} for sufficiently large k and small t > 0, refuting the earlier stability conjectures and giving upper bounds on the largest n for which all matrices in each class are stable. However, the exact value of the largest n with guaranteed stability for each of the four classes does not appear to have been pinned down; the precise threshold remains open as far as available sources indicate.

status_evidence.title: Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable
status_evidence.snippet: A class of unstable GKK τ-matrices A_{2k+2,k,t} is constructed, disproving the stability conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit unstable GKK τ-matrices exist, so the largest stability dimension is finite, but the exact maximum is not stated.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on GKK τ-matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Several open problems concerning stability of subclasses C_n of GKK and τ-matrices are posed.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of determining the largest n with guaranteed stability for these classes is explicitly posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Theorems and counterexamples on structured matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys results on GKK and τ-matrices, including instability constructions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides constructions bounding but not exactly determining the maximal stable dimension.
